author: Rinehart
text:
Price didn't come near the area before bedtime so I just put on a
reduced risk set and forget trade. If I was awake, I would have been
happy with this approach. IF has said that nothing brings retail into a
 bad trade like a fast move. If price had consolidated and then
compressed up to my entry, that would scare me more because IT can
change out their orders in a situation like that.

Set, forget and sleep is difficult to embrace, but it does wonders for
saving my emotions during trades. Plus, it gives me a built in risk
monitor. If I can't sleep / keep opening my laptop / looking at my
phone. I'm risking too much and I need to close some positions.

author: haanz
text: Hi Ryan, your chart show that you use trendline to assist your analysis in ENG. Do you use ENG of FL + Trendline?

author: Rinehart
text:
NO, they are two unrelated types of analysis.

Before RTM I was a pattern trader. The pattern I drew is called a
rising wedge. It is supposed to be bearish on the break of the lower
trendline. However, I liked to trade them when they faked out the upper
 trendline and closed below it. They can perform very well, but
sometimes they fail like everything else in trading. However, because I
 had a rising wedge which is bearish and I had an engulf. I felt
confident about the market wanting to reverse.
